## Week 2, Session 1 — One-way ANOVA and contrasts (emmeans) {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans}

<div class="callout callout-note">
**Inference labs** use the five-step template:
Hypothesis → Visualise → Assumptions → Conduct → Conclude.
</div>

### Learning objectives {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-learning-objectives}

- Fit a one-way ANOVA with `aov()` and interpret the omnibus *F*-test.
- Use `emmeans` to obtain estimated marginal means and pairwise
  contrasts with controlled family-wise error.
- Read a Tukey HSD output and translate it into a sentence.

### Prerequisites {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-prerequisites}

t-tests; linear regression basics.

### Background {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-background}

Analysis of variance is linear regression with a categorical predictor
and a tradition. The omnibus *F*-test asks whether any group means
differ; the follow-up contrasts ask which ones. The correct order is
omnibus first, then targeted contrasts, preferably with a multiple
testing correction that respects the family of tests you intended
before seeing the data.

The `emmeans` package has made the post-hoc machinery substantially
cleaner. `emmeans(fit, ~ group)` returns the estimated marginal means
on the response scale; `pairs()` produces the pairwise differences
with Tukey-adjusted *p*-values by default.

A common mistake is to run pairwise *t*-tests without correction and
report the one with the smallest *p*-value. A less common but more
insidious mistake is to run the omnibus *F*, see it is significant, and
stop — reporting a single *p*-value without naming which groups
differ and by how much.

### Setup {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-setup}

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(emmeans)
set.seed(42)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

### 1. Hypothesis {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-1-hypothesis}

Using `ToothGrowth`, ask whether guinea-pig tooth length depends on
dose of vitamin C.

Null: mean tooth length is equal across the three doses.
Alternative: at least one dose differs.

### 2. Visualise {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-2-visualise}

```r
tg <- ToothGrowth |> mutate(dose = factor(dose))
ggplot(tg, aes(dose, len, fill = dose)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, colour = "grey30") +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg/day)", y = "Tooth length") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### 3. Assumptions {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-3-assumptions}

Approximate normality within groups and equal variances.

```r
fit <- aov(len ~ dose, data = tg)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(fit)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
bartlett.test(len ~ dose, data = tg)
```

### 4. Conduct {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-4-conduct}

```r
summary(fit)

emm <- emmeans(fit, ~ dose)
emm
pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey")
```

### 5. Concluding statement {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-5-concluding-statement}

> Tooth length increased with dose of vitamin C (one-way ANOVA
> *F* = `round(summary(fit)[[1]]$"F value"[1], 2)`; *p* =
> `signif(summary(fit)[[1]]$"Pr(>F)"[1], 2)`). Tukey-adjusted
> contrasts indicated that the 2 mg/day dose gave longer teeth than
> both lower doses (all adjusted *p* < 0.05).


### Common pitfalls {#sec-chapters-07-regression-labs-lab-one-way-anova-and-contrasts-emmeans-common-pitfalls}

- Stopping at a significant *F* without reporting which contrasts drive
  it.
- Reporting unadjusted pairwise *p*-values after the omnibus test.
- Treating a non-significant Bartlett test as proof of equal variances.
